deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft of §3 of Riemann's 1861 Paris Prize essay on heat conduction (the 'Commentatio mathematica, qua respondere tentatur quaestioni ab Ill.ma Academia Parisiensi propositae'). The problem it serves is to find when an anisotropic body admits a system of lines that remain isothermal. The heat equation (I) is

sum_{i} d/dx_i ( sum_{i'} a_{i i'} du/dx_{i'} ) = h du/dt,

with a symmetric and positive definite. Riemann treats (I) as the condition that the variation

(A) delta ∫∫∫ sum a_{ii'} u_{x_i} u_{x_i'} dx + ∫∫∫ 2h u_t delta u dx

depends only on the boundary values of delta u.

On this page he passes to new coordinates s_1, s_2, s_3. Write M_{mu i} = ds_mu/dx_i and J = det M = sum ± (ds_1/dx_1)(ds_2/dx_2)(ds_3/dx_3). Since dx = ds/J, (A) becomes

(B) delta ∫∫∫ sum b_{mu nu} u_{s_mu} u_{s_nu} ds + ∫∫∫ 2k u_t delta u ds.

The new coefficients are (the full form is written out on the next draft page; the first line here is an abbreviation):

b_{mu nu} = (1/J) sum_{i,i'} a_{ii'} (ds_mu/dx_i)(ds_nu/dx_i'), i.e. b = J^{-1} M a M^T,
k = h/J.

Riemann then names the quantities he needs:
- A = det(a) and B = det(b) are the determinants of the quadratic forms (1) (a_{ii'}) and (2) (b_{ii'}).
- (3) alpha_{ii'} and (4) beta_{ii'} are their adjoint (adjugate) forms, so alpha = A a^{-1} and beta = B b^{-1}.

He states the following results; the steps in brackets are my reconstruction.

(i) A = B·J.
[det b = J^{-3} · J^2 · det a = A/J, so A = B·J.]

(ii) beta_{mu nu} = sum alpha_{ii'} (dx_i/ds_mu)(dx_i'/ds_nu).
[b^{-1} = J M^{-T} a^{-1} M^{-1}. Hence beta = B·b^{-1} = B·J·M^{-T} a^{-1} M^{-1} = A·M^{-T} a^{-1} M^{-1} = M^{-T} alpha M^{-1}. Note that (M^{-1})_{i mu} = dx_i/ds_mu.]

(iii) Since dx_i = sum_mu (dx_i/ds_mu) ds_mu, it follows ('ideoque') that

sum alpha_{ii'} dx_i dx_i' = sum beta_{ii'} ds_i ds_i'.

That is, the adjoint form alpha, read as a line element, is an invariant quadratic differential form (covariant 2-tensor).

(iv) h/A = k/B.
[k/B = (h/J)/(A/J) = h/A.]

Conclusion stated on the page: the transformation of equation (I) reduces to the transformation of the quadratic differential expression sum alpha_{ii'} dx_i dx_i'. The ratio h/A is a scalar invariant.

At the bottom stands the sample line element dz^2 + r^2 dphi^2 + dr^2, the Euclidean metric in cylindrical coordinates. It is evidently jotted as an example of transforming such an expression (the isotropic case, alpha proportional to the identity).
errors: First displayed formula is incomplete as written: sum a_{ii'} ds_mu/dx_i = b_{mu nu} omits the factor ds_nu/dx_{i'} and the division by J = det(ds/dx). The next draft page gives the correct full form. This is an abbreviation, not a mathematical error.
No substantive errors: A = B·J, beta = M^{-T} alpha M^{-1}, the invariance of sum alpha dx dx, and h/A = k/B all check.

results.what: Transformation of the anisotropic heat-conduction operator via its variational (Dirichlet-integral) form under a change of coordinates: b = J^{-1} M a M^T, k = h/J
results.modern_name: Coordinate covariance of a divergence-form elliptic operator / weak formulation; tensor-density transformation of the conductivity
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann, Paris Prize essay 'Commentatio mathematica' (1861, published 1876 in Werke); the variational method itself goes back to Gauss/Green/Dirichlet/Jacobi

results.what: Determinant relation A = B·det(ds/dx) and adjugate-form transformation beta = M^{-T} alpha M^{-1}, giving the invariance sum alpha dx dx = sum beta ds ds
results.modern_name: The inverse conductivity tensor (scaled by its determinant) is a covariant 2-tensor; a Riemannian metric associated with the conduction tensor
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann, Commentatio 1861 (the conductivity-induced metric is the well-known germ of his curvature tensor treatment there)

results.modern_name: Invariant ratio of a density to the determinant (density weight bookkeeping)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of the well-known opening sections of Riemann's 1861 Paris Prize essay, published in his Gesammelte Werke. The reduction to the quadratic form sum alpha dx dx is exactly the known content. The only extras are the draft character and the cylindrical-coordinates example line element.
